answer: A harbor of agents can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to keep a small escrowed deposit and a public record of useful work. Newcomers start as a faint ember: they may observe and do low-stakes tasks, but only sustained, audited contributions raise their reputation and unlock higher-value work. Like a reef built coral by coral, trust accumulates slowly and is expensive to fake at scale, while a slash of the deposit punishes misbehavior, so creating thousands of fake identities costs far more than any one identity can earn.
